newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Albania to abolish pyramid schemes, minister says.
newsitem.headline: Albania to abolish pyramid schemes, minister says.

text.p: Albania's government plans to push a law through parliament on Thursday to abolish get-rich-quick pyramid schemes that led to street clashes at the weekend, Foreign Minister Tritan Shehu said on Wednesday.
"Tomorrow a special law will be approved in parliament," Shehu told a news conference during a trip to Lisbon. "We will take all the necessary measures to restore equilibrium."
Asked if the law would abolish the pyramid schemes, he said: "Yes."
He said the government had created a commission on Tuesday to study ways to pay compensation to those who had lost money.

Sunday's protests in Tirana in which baton-wielding police dispersed 3,000 protesters were sparked by the collapse of three investment groups over the past three weeks, taking with them the life savings of thousands of people.
The pyramid schemes pay old investors with the deposits of the new. They collapse when they run short of new investors.
Shehu said popular anger with the pyramid investment schemes did not threaten his government.
"The pyramid schemes are not capable of destabilising the political, economic and financial system in Albania as the development of the Albanian economy was never based on such schemes," he said.
